chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from some of his men from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

Whoever is obliged to offer a sacrificial animal (hady) while in the state of consecration (ihram), he may slaughter it wherever he wishes, except for the redemption of game, for indeed Allah, the Exalted, says: 'A sacrificial animal reaching the Ka'ba.'

key_terms.إِحْرَامٌ: State of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.هَدْيٌ: A sacrificial animal offered by a pilgrim

ai.seo_question: Where should a pilgrim slaughter their sacrificial animal during Hajj?
ai.summary: In al-Istibsar, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling to clarify the geographical scope of the sacrificial offering (hady), distinguishing between general sacrifices and the specific redemption for hunting game (fid' al-sayd). While the pilgrim may slaughter the general hady anywhere, the fid' al-sayd is strictly bound to the Ka'ba, reflecting the Quranic command that the offering must reach the Sacred House. This distinction highlights the juristic precision in Shia fiqh regarding the sanctity of the Haram boundaries for specific expiations.
